cards.explanation: The answer is that Elisha will not leave Elijah. Elisha, the man chosen to take over from Elijah the prophet (1 Kings 19:16), says, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." That's not a maybe, friends. He puts an oath on it. Elijah asked nicely and got a promise back, so they went down to Bethel together.

The answer is that they ask if he knows the LORD will take his master today. The sons of the prophets, a group of prophets at Bethel, come out and ask, "Do you know that the LORD will take your master away from you today?" The master is Elijah. They bring up the news, and the news is about today. That's a big thing to hear on a walk.

The answer is False. Elisha doesn't act surprised at all. He answers, "Yes, I know…" and then says, "Do not speak of it." He already knew, and he was walking on anyway. I think that tells you a lot about him, friends.

The answer is the Jordan. Elijah says, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me on to the Jordan." Bethel, then Jericho, then the river. Elijah keeps saying it's the LORD sending him. And yes, Elisha keeps walking.

The answer is True. Elisha says the same words a third time: "As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." Three asks, three answers, and the answer never changed, bakers. So the two of them went on.

The answer is that Elijah strikes the waters. He took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters. The river did the rest, because the waters parted. A rolled up cloak is not much of a tool, but that is what he used. Friends, I can't even get the dough to leave my rolling pin.
The answer is dry. The waters part to the right and to the left, and the two of them cross "…on dry ground." The riverbed isn't wet at all. That's a good way to cross a river, friends. No wet shoes.

The answer is a double portion of Elijah's spirit. Elisha says, "Please, let me inherit a double portion of your spirit…" Elijah had asked what he could do for him before being taken away, and that's the answer he got. I would've asked for a bigger oven, bakers. Elisha asked for something far better.

The answer is False. Elijah says, "You have requested a difficult thing…" He doesn't call it easy. But he doesn't shut the door, either. He adds, "Nevertheless, if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours."

The answer is that he must see Elijah taken from him. Elijah says, "…if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours. But if not, then it will not be so." So Elisha has to be watching. Good thing he wasn't going anywhere, friends.

The answer is separated. A chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them. Elijah and Elisha were walking and talking, and then they weren't together anymore. Then Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.

The answer is True. The text says, "As Elisha watched…" he cried out, and then he saw Elijah no more. That matters, friends, because Elijah had said that if Elisha saw him taken, it would be his (2 Kings 2:10). Elisha was watching.
The answer is that he tears them in two. The text says, "…taking hold of his own clothes, he tore them in two." Elisha had just seen Elijah no more. I think this was a heavy moment for him, friends.

The answer is that he asks where the LORD, the God of Elijah, is now. Elisha strikes the waters with Elijah's cloak and asks, "Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" Elijah is out of sight, and the question isn't about Elijah. It's about the LORD. Then the waters part to the right and to the left, and Elisha crosses over.

The answer is True. When he struck the waters, "…they parted to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over." It's the same thing that happened for Elijah earlier, friends. Elisha did it alone this time.

The answer is that the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha. The sons of the prophets, watching from Jericho, say, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They saw what happened at the river, and that was their conclusion. Then they went to meet him.

The answer is True. The text says the sons of the prophets went to meet him and "…bowed down to the ground before him." That comes after they said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They had been watching from Jericho when it all happened at the river, friends.
The answer is that Elisha says, "Do not send them…" The sons of the prophets had offered fifty valiant men to search. Elisha said no the first time they asked, bakers.

The answer is three days. The fifty men "…searched for three days but did not find Elijah." Three days is a long time to search and come back with nothing. I bet those were some tired feet, friends. Elisha had said not to send them, and he reminded them when they got back.
The answer is False. The fifty men "…searched for three days but did not find Elijah." Elisha had told them not to send anyone. When they came back, he said, "Didn’t I tell you not to go?"

The answer is salt. Elisha says, "Bring me a new bowl, and put some salt in it." Then he goes out to the spring and casts the salt into it. It's a simple thing, friends, salt in a bowl. And he says, "This is what the LORD says: 'I have healed this water…'"

The answer is the LORD. Elisha says, "This is what the LORD says: ‘I have healed this water. No longer will it cause death or unfruitfulness.’…" The word came from the LORD, friends. Elisha is the one speaking it.

The answer is False. The text says, "…the waters there have been healthy to this day, according to the word spoken by Elisha." The water didn't go bad again. Elisha had said, "No longer will it cause death or unfruitfulness." Not a bad spring since, bakers.

The answer is that he calls down a curse in the LORD's name. The text says he turned around, looked at them, and "…called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD." This is a heavy part of the story, friends. Right after that, two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.
